title: The completed adic Roos fibre kills strict pro-zero cones
statement: For a scheme T and completed adic coefficient datum d, take the actual completed module sheaves and strict towers of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. If a map v of complexes of strict towers has a cone whose levelwise transition maps eventually become zero in the derived category of completed module sheaves, then the concrete Roos fibre map of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison] induced by v is a quasi-isomorphism. No Koszul, finite quotient, or K-flat hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 0940 and 0941, exact products and countable derived inverse limit; pro-zero tower vanishing

proof.text: The pro-etale countable-products theorem says the product of epimorphisms of completed module sheaves is epi. Express a limit map for a discrete countable diagram through Pi.isoLimit and Pi.map, obtaining preservation of epimorphisms by the limit functor and hence exact countable products.

Use the derived evaluation isomorphism of the ringed strict derived-limit theorem. Its naturality and cancellation along its component isomorphisms transfer the given eventually zero transition maps to eventually zero maps of the derived cone tower. The pro-zero clause gives invertibility of the derived-limit map.

The exact-products comparison identifies the concrete Roos model with that derived-limit functor. Naturality transports invertibility of the induced map, and the derived-category criterion identifies it with quasi-isomorphy of the original concrete Roos map.

theorem completedAdicRoosMapQuasiIsoOfProZero
    (T : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    {X Y : CochainComplex (CompletedAdicTowers T d) ℤ} (v : X ⟶ Y)
    (hv : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m), DerivedCategory.Q.map
      ((CochainComplex.mappingCone v).asFunctor.map (homOfLE h).op) = 0) :
    QuasiIso (ExactProductsRoos.fibre.map v)
